details:
Q1: How will the required `files_touched` grant get into this issue body? It must be in the body, not a comment, and authored or edited by a trusted account.
Choices:
A: A repository operator edits this issue body and adds a `- files_touched:` block listing the exact paths from Q2, then removes any `ai:scope-blocked` label and re-runs the pipeline. (RECOMMENDED)
B: Close this issue and have the pipeline account file a replacement whose body already contains the `- files_touched:` block.
C: Shrink the change so it touches no automation paths (`scripts/`, `.github/`, `prompts/`, `.claude/`, `workflow-templates/`). **Note:** this can't work. The flag gate has to live in `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh` / `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`, and choosing C will bounce back for re-clarification.
Q2: Which exact paths should the grant list? Entries must be exact, with no globs or trailing `/`. The general `files_touched` guard also applies to paths outside the automation directories, so list every file.
Choices:
A: `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh`, `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`, `tests/test_review_conflict_resolve_sandbox_only.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `README.md`, `changelog.d/6806-conflict-hook-template-resolve.md` (RECOMMENDED)
B: Option A plus `.github/workflows/review_autofix.yml`, to forward the flag as a repo variable. The helper's own default of `false` still applies (§8).
C: Option A without `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, if the existing CI step already collects the test file without registering it.
